The inverse is the one in source68-71. Differentiating the actual49 once gives D1[u]=B(u-H D1[u]) and therefore D1=RB. Differentiating it again, for fixed directions u,v, gives

    (I+B H) D''(A)[u,v]=Ccal''(F(A))[T u,T v],
    D''(A)[u,v]=R Ccal''(F(A))[T u,T v].        (I)

No term differentiating H appears in(I), because this is the A-derivative at FIXED U0, as required for189. A derivative in the external background or later history would have additional H/J terms and is not being calculated here.

Write C_F=Ccal''(F(A)) and C_0=Ccal''(0). Since D1(0)=0, R(0)=I and T(0)=I, D2''=C_0. Consequently the actual cubic-and-higher remainder has the exact decomposition

     +(C_F-C_0)[T u,T v]

Also R-I=-R B H. The last positive mixed term in(II) is essential. The two negative terms alone would double-subtract the product contribution. Every term in(II) vanishes at A=0, keeping the quadratic current contribution in78/79 rather than counting it again as a nonlinear term.
